name: Founder sales pipeline
summary: Sell as the founder without losing the thread of your conversations. A short pipeline from first conversation to won, with an optional pilot that has an end date and a parked state with a date to come back.
description: When you sell personally, every conversation teaches you who buys and why, but the notes and the next step live in your head and a stack of tabs. This template keeps a handful to a few dozen open conversations: each opportunity records the problem in the customer's words, urgency, budget status and whether the decision maker is engaged. A pilot has an end date and says whether it is paid, and a quiet deal is parked with a date to revisit instead of being chased. Weights are rough, since a founder has no close-rate history yet, and they are yours to set. It is not outbound sequencing at volume, fundraising or a forecast for a team with several sellers.

page.headline: Founder-led sales without losing the thread: your AI agent builds the pipeline in your CRM
page.answer: A founder-led sales pipeline is a short list of open conversations, each with the problem in the customer's words, a dated next step and, where you run one, a pilot with a fixed end date. Paste this template into your AI agent and it builds the pipeline in Customermates, with a parked state and a date to come back to quiet deals. You approve the plan before anything is built.

routine.title: The Monday founder review
steps: List every open conversation and give each one a dated next step. A conversation without a date is the one that goes quiet.
Write down what you learned since last week: the problem in the buyer's words, urgency, budget and who decides.
Check the pilots: is the end date set, are the success criteria written, is it paid? Hold the decision call a few days before it ends.
Decide about the quiet deals: send one honest closing message, then park them with a date to come back instead of chasing.
Look at who bought and who said no, and why. The pattern shows which segment to sell to, and when it is time to hire your first salesperson.

limits: It is not outbound sequencing. Customermates has no sequences or mass outreach, and each message is individual and reviewed by you. LinkedIn or email at volume needs a specialist tool.
It is not an investor CRM. Fundraising has other stages and counterparties, so use a separate template for it.
It makes no quotes, invoices or contracts and has no e-signature. Proposals and agreements are made in other tools; only the dates and a link live here.
There is no lead scoring or data enrichment. How well a lead fits is a field you set yourself.
Weighted value is not a forecast. The weights are rough, because a founder has no close-rate history yet, and they are yours to change.
It is sized for one seller. Several salespeople with quotas and a team forecast need the sales pipeline template or a heavier CRM.

faq.question: When does a founder need a CRM?
faq.answer: Guides put it at the point where you have more leads and customers than fit in your head or a spreadsheet, often somewhere between 50 and 200 contacts, or when a second person starts to sell. A sheet is enough until then. The cost of waiting is that notes and next steps are already scattered when you do switch.

faq.question: How many customers should a founder close personally?
faq.answer: Advice differs: Jason Lemkin says the first 10 customers, maybe 20, other guides say 10 to 50. Mercury says to hire your first salesperson when you can say 'I know I can sell my product to people like X who have problem Y'. The template shows how many customers you have won and does not enforce a number.

faq.question: How long should I chase a quiet deal?
faq.answer: Practitioners disagree on the number but agree that you stop at some point. Mercury advises to stop chasing prospects who ignore you, others suggest a few follow-ups, a last email and a contact months later. The template does both: one closing message, then the deal is parked with a revisit date 90 days out.

faq.question: Should I run a free pilot?
faq.answer: Advice summarised from Y Combinator's Startup School is to avoid open-ended free pilots and to run a short, scored, ideally paid one. The template gives a pilot a fixed end date and a flag for paid or unpaid, creates a check-in 14 days after it starts and an Action for the decision call 3 days before it ends.

faq.question: Does the agent send messages to my prospects?
faq.answer: No. The prompt tells the agent to send nothing and to create no sample records. Drafts exist only when you ask for them, and you send them yourself.

prompt.intro: I sell my product myself and keep losing the notes and next steps from my conversations. Set up a founder sales pipeline in my Customermates workspace: opportunities from the first conversation to won with discovery notes, an optional pilot with a fixed end date, a parked state with a revisit date, and dated follow-ups. Send nothing automatically.
questions: What do you sell, and who has bought from you so far?
Do you run pilots or trials, and are they paid?
How long do you chase a quiet deal before you park it?
Where do your conversations start: your network, introductions, inbound or events?
